title: Count the Number of Good Partitions
summary: Given an array of positive integers, determine the count of all possible partitions where each subarray contains unique numbers, modulo 10^9 + 7.
statement: Given an array of positive integers, determine the count of all possible partitions where each subarray contains unique numbers, modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Partition nums into contiguous nonempty groups so every distinct value occurs in only one group.
Return the number of valid partitions modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: A cut is legal only after every value seen in the current block has reached its last occurrence.
Track the farthest last occurrence while scanning.
Each index reaching that frontier closes one forced atomic block; choose cuts between adjacent blocks.
Values cannot cross atomic boundaries, while any subset of the block gaps is valid, giving 2^(blocks-1).
editorial: Values cannot cross atomic boundaries, while any subset of the block gaps is valid, giving 2^(blocks-1).

All occurrences must remain together, so only one partition is valid.
